scope: Observed local Linux x86-64 installations using JDK 22, Kotlin 2.2.0, kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm 1.8.0, Maven 3.9.11, Lean 4.32.2 and the local glibc 2.36 override. Retained callbacks have copied scalar arguments and replies; the enclosing task can borrow and return a direct resource. Not hosted CI, registry publication, or closure of all languages/ownership shapes.
checks: An ordinary and a reviewed Depot JAR each resolved through an offline Maven repository with its original, independently built Desk peer and same-named incompatible OtherDesk type. Verified every original JAR entry, POM, runtime/ledger/native owner dependency and the shared nominal class bytes before compiling relocated Java and Kotlin clients. Both languages reject both wrong kinds and same-spelling foreign definitions.

Real Lean workers keep borrowed inputs alive after host close, mutate the same object and return independently disposable leases. Covered successful and rejected factories, resource-bearing callback tasks and original host exceptions, blocked callback cancellation, cooperative and late workers, pull demand, stream exhaustion, early cancel, typed step failure, post-retirement cleanup without running user close code. Test processes ended with zero live identities, no residual Lean file descriptors and no readiness reactor.

Additional ordinary/reviewed Java and Kotlin clients closed the last host lease while a pending worker or an already-open cursor still held the file. With no host resource lease, a pending worker held two broker identities (delivery handle and completion notification). Non-cooperative cancellation removed the delivery handle immediately, leaving one notification and the file until the worker finished; then broker identities, file descriptors and reactor count returned to baseline. A fresh cold Java subscription after closing the sole input was rejected without invalidating the open cursor.

A test-only package peer pauses the installed native port after a real take/decoding but before production settlement. Verified cancel and external future completion dispose only unpublished native leases; a caller-supplied replacement remains usable. Invalid demand or cancellation after a native stream take or owned step failure disposes the unused lease. A controlled Kotlin dispatcher exercises pending success and typed-error signals at the actual coroutine handoff, including unconsumed channel elements; cancellation does not revoke a caller-owned exception from a retained callback.

Both source review mutations (wrong stream-step payload and read-only borrow in place of a mutable borrow) are refused without any output release. An offline-installed CLI reproduced the complete ordinary Maven handoff. The current generator was also compared to every generated source file in the original accepted scalar task, retained callback and synchronous-resource packages without rebuilding old commits.
reproduce: Use JDK 22, Kotlin 2.2.0, Maven 3.9.11, Python 3.11+, unzip/readelf and Lean 4.32.2 as in docs/evidence/jvm-tasks-20261123.json. Seed LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_TASK_M2_SEED with third-party prerequisites only, LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1. Set LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_LEASE_TASK_SYNC to the original handoffs from jvm-sync-resources-20261123.json. Use fresh EVIDENCE and SECOND destinations; only use the 2.36 floor override on the matching local platform.

LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_LEASE_TASK_ORIGINAL=$EVIDENCE LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_LEASE_SOLE_OUTPUT=$EVIDENCE/sole.json node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/helpers/jvm-lease-tasks-sole.mjs (for replay set LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_LEASE_TASK_EXPECTED to this receipt and use a new output file).
LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_ORIGINAL=$EVIDENCE LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_REPRO=$SECOND node --test --test-name-pattern='offline-installed CLI in a second producer' tests/helpers/jvm-io-installed.mjs

Set LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_PRIOR_TASK and LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_PRIOR_CALLBACK to original scalar-task and retained-callback handoffs. LEAN_BRIDGE_JVM_LEASE_TASK_COMPAT=$EVIDENCE/compat.json node --test tests/helpers/jvm-lease-tasks-compat.mjs
